newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mergers set new record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mergers set new record in 1996.

text.p: U.S. mergers and acquisitions set a record in 1996 despite initial predictions that the pace of transactions would not exceed 1995's record, according to two surveys released Tuesday.
Securities Data Co., a Newark, N.J.-based company that tracks merger activity, said $658.8 billion worth of transactions were announced in 1996, up from the 1995 record of $519 billion.
Meanwhile, Mergerstat Review, a division of investment bank Houlihan Lokey Howard & Zukin, estimated $492.9 billion in total transactions for 1996, up 37 percent from 1995 levels.

The two firms use different methodology for compiling merger data. Securities Data Co. figures incluse asset sales and the purchase of small equity stakes. Mergerstat Review tracks transactions that involve U.S. companies and does not include the exchange of business assets or spin-offs.

Telecommunications companies rung up the year's biggest deals, including unions between British Telecommunications Plc. and MCI Communications Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp. and NYNEX Corp., and SBC Communications Inc.'s and Pacific Telesis Group.
Utilities were another hot sector, but the pace of bank transactions, slowed sharply from 1995.
Mergerstat Review found 94 transactions valued at $1 billion or more, accounting for 59 percent of the overall merger market in 1996.
Mergerstat also said that U.S. companies announced 5,859 transactions in 1996, up 67 percent from 1995.
In the fourth quarter, some $201.7 billion worth of deals were announced, including Boeing Co.'s $13.3 billion offer for McDonnell Douglas Corp., according to Securities Data.
In early 1996, many merger experts predicted the year's activity would hold below 1995 levels, but a strong stock market kept transactions at a strong pace.
